macroIntelligence.marketBias: Middle East energy-supply risk remains elevated. Reuters reports the Iran-Oman understanding does not provide for immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, while a Monday Oman meeting is expected to continue talks without a signed deal. Combined with the Saudi East-West pipeline shutdown, Red Sea disruption, oil above $100 and near-term Fed/ECB tightening risk, the overlay remains PREPARE VOLATILITY with no intelligence-only buy or sell trigger.

items.headline: Iran-Oman understanding does not provide for immediate reopening of Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Reuters reports an Iranian source said the Iran-Oman understanding lays groundwork for a possible future reopening of Hormuz but does not provide for immediate reopening. A separate Reuters report says Monday's Oman meeting is not expected to produce a signed Hormuz deal.
items.whyItMatters: Failure to reopen Hormuz promptly prolongs the oil-supply, inflation, yields and risk-liquidity shock affecting crypto and other risk assets.
items.actionReason: This materially confirms persistence of the energy shock, but it is not a direct crypto protocol failure and does not independently justify REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW.

items.headline: Trump says Iran probably responsible for attack on Saudi East-West oil pipeline
items.summary: Reuters reports President Donald Trump said Iran was probably responsible for the aerial attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline after speaking with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The attribution is not proof of responsibility, but it raises escalation risk around already-disrupted Middle East energy infrastructure.
items.whyItMatters: Direct U.S. political attribution can increase retaliation and escalation risk, potentially extending the oil, inflation, yields and risk-liquidity shock affecting crypto.
items.actionReason: Material escalation risk, but responsibility remains unverified and this is not a direct crypto protocol failure; no independent REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW trigger.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia shuts East-West oil pipeline after drone attack as Houthis seize Perim Island
items.summary: Reuters reports Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its East-West pipeline after a drone attack originating from Iraq, while Iran-aligned Houthis seized Perim Island at the mouth of the Red Sea. The pipeline had been moving roughly 4-5 million barrels per day, about 4-5% of global supply, and the combined disruptions tighten both Hormuz-bypass capacity and Bab el-Mandeb shipping risk.
items.whyItMatters: A simultaneous threat to Saudi overland bypass capacity and Red Sea transit can intensify the existing energy shock, lift inflation expectations and yields, and tighten global risk-asset liquidity including crypto.
items.actionReason: This is a material escalation of the existing macro/energy risk regime, but it is not a direct crypto protocol failure and does not independently justify REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW.

items.headline: Oil tanker freight rates hit record highs as Middle East shipping attacks tighten capacity
items.summary: Reuters reports VLCC rates from the Gulf of Oman to China reached a record Worldscale 450, equivalent to roughly $11.50 per barrel, after attacks on shipping reduced available tanker capacity. Persistently elevated freight costs can amplify the existing energy-price shock and feed broader inflation pressure.
items.whyItMatters: Record physical oil-transport costs reinforce the inflation and financial-conditions channel already weighing on global risk assets and crypto liquidity.
items.actionReason: This materially extends the existing energy/logistics shock but does not independently justify REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW.

items.headline: ECB policymakers open door to further rate hikes if energy shock persists
items.summary: Reuters reports Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel and Estonia's central bank governor Ulo Kaasik signaled further ECB rate increases may be needed if energy prices keep feeding inflation; money markets are pricing at least three more ECB hikes over the next year.
items.whyItMatters: A broader global tightening cycle can keep yields and funding conditions restrictive for crypto even after the U.S. CPI event has passed.
items.actionReason: The hawkish follow-through extends the existing restrictive-liquidity regime but does not independently justify REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW.

items.headline: U.S. August CPI accelerates; markets price roughly 85% chance of a Fed hike next week
items.summary: Reuters reports headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m and 3.4% y/y in August, both in line with consensus, while core CPI rose 0.3% m/m and 2.4% y/y. Subsequent market reporting put the implied probability of a 25 bp Fed hike next week near 85%, up from about 67% before the data, with the U.S. 10-year yield briefly reaching 4.9915%.
items.whyItMatters: The CPI release resolves the scheduled event but materially increases near-term tightening expectations and keeps yields near 5%, which can pressure crypto liquidity and risk appetite.
items.actionReason: The <=2h CPI AVOID NEW ENTRY window has expired, but post-release Fed repricing and near-5% yields remain a material volatility risk. This does not independently justify REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW.

items.headline: IEA warns 2026 oil supply gap will widen as normal Gulf flows are delayed
items.summary: Reuters reports the IEA now expects global oil supply to decline by about 5.7 million b/d in 2026 as Middle East disruptions persist, with Saudi output at multi-decade lows and global inventories under pressure.
items.whyItMatters: A deeper and more persistent energy supply shock can keep inflation expectations and bond yields elevated, tightening financial conditions for crypto and other risk assets.
items.actionReason: Material macro risk extension; it does not independently justify REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW.

items.headline: Brent retreats from $109.97 peak but remains above $100 as supply risk persists
items.summary: Reuters reports Brent fell to about $105.17 by 16:33 GMT after reports of possible temporary talks on Hormuz shipping, reversing part of its earlier surge to $109.97. It still remained on track for a weekly gain above 9%, with major supply disruptions unresolved.
items.whyItMatters: The pullback reduces immediate inflation panic but oil above $100 and unresolved shipping disruptions keep volatility and restrictive-rates risk elevated.
items.actionReason: This is a partial reversal of the intraday oil spike, not a resolution of the broader supply shock; no independent REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW trigger.

items.headline: Brent settles at $107.63 and WTI at $102.48 as tanker attacks deepen supply disruption
items.summary: Reuters reports Brent settled at $107.63 and WTI at $102.48 after further tanker attacks and disruption around Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure. This extends the existing HIGH oil/inflation/rates risk regime rather than creating a separate new catalyst.
items.whyItMatters: Persistent triple pressure from oil, yields and tighter policy expectations can constrain crypto liquidity and increase downside volatility.
items.actionReason: The settlement extends the already-recorded macro risk regime but does not independently justify REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW.

items.headline: Brent reaches $105.26 and WTI moves above $100 as tanker attacks escalate
items.summary: Reuters reports Brent rose about 4% to $105.26 and WTI moved above $100 for the first time since May as attacks on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea intensified. The escalation extends the oil-supply shock and increases inflation, yields and risk-asset volatility pressure.
items.whyItMatters: A renewed oil spike above $100 for both Brent and WTI can lift inflation expectations and bond yields and tighten financial conditions for crypto and other risk assets.
items.actionReason: This is a material macro escalation but not a direct crypto protocol failure and does not independently justify REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW.

items.headline: ECB raises deposit rate by 25 bp to 2.50%
items.summary: Reuters reports the ECB raised its deposit rate to 2.50%, its second hike of 2026, as energy-driven inflation remains above target. The decision tightens European financial conditions.
items.whyItMatters: A higher ECB policy rate can pressure global risk assets through yields, FX and tighter financial conditions.
items.actionReason: The scheduled decision is resolved; post-decision repricing can still produce volatility.

items.headline: US August PPI rises 0.4% m/m and 5.4% y/y
items.summary: Reuters reports U.S. producer prices rose 0.4% in August, in line with market expectations, while the annual rate increased to 5.4% from 4.8% in July. Energy prices rose 4.2%, keeping inflation and Fed-rate sensitivity elevated ahead of CPI.
items.whyItMatters: The monthly print was expected, limiting surprise risk, but the higher annual rate and energy contribution keep inflation pressure material for Fed expectations and crypto liquidity.
items.actionReason: The event is resolved; post-release macro conditions remain restrictive.

items.headline: Oman-hosted Iran-Gulf talks on Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Reuters reports Oman plans to host Iran and Gulf states on Monday for talks including Hormuz governance, but an Iranian official said no signed deal is expected at the meeting. The exact meeting time was not reported in the verified source.
items.whyItMatters: Any credible path toward reopening Hormuz could reduce energy and inflation pressure; failure or escalation could prolong the shock. The outcome can materially move oil, yields and crypto risk sentiment.
items.actionReason: Reliable HIGH catalyst inside seven days, but the exact time is unknown so no <=6h or <=2h event window is asserted.

items.headline: U.S. Senate procedural vote on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act
items.summary: Reuters reports the Senate is set for a pivotal procedural vote on the Clarity Act on September 15; the vote concerns whether the Senate proceeds with the digital-asset market-structure bill, not final passage.
items.whyItMatters: The vote can materially alter expectations for U.S. crypto market-structure regulation and therefore regulatory risk premia across major digital assets.
items.actionReason: HIGH regulatory catalyst inside seven days but not yet inside the six-hour notification window.

items.headline: Federal Reserve FOMC rate decision, SEP and press conference
items.summary: The Federal Reserve calendar confirms the two-day FOMC meeting on September 15-16, with the policy decision at 2:00 p.m. ET and press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET on September 16.
items.whyItMatters: The rate decision and projections can materially reset yields, the dollar and global crypto liquidity.
items.actionReason: Reliable HIGH catalyst inside the next seven days but not yet inside the 24-hour volatility window.
